claim: Let \(G=(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^3\). A nonempty subset \(A\subset G\) pd-tiles \(G\) weakly if and only if \(|A|\in\{1,2,4,8\}\). Equivalently, every positive-definite weak tile of \(G\) is a translational tile, so \(G\) is pd-flat.
integrity: The proof uses exact finite-group arguments. The exhaustive checker independently replays all 255 nonempty subsets; no numerical approximation is used for the theorem.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to \((\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^3\).
It does not classify unrestricted weak tiles without the positive-definiteness condition.
Differently phrased or non-indexed literature remains a residual originality risk.
title: Complete positive-definite weak-tiling classification of \((\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^3\)
